entries.title: Micah 3:1
segments: Corrupt rulers and corrupt teachers generally go together, and they strengthen each other in wickedness.  When they who are appointed to administer justice to the people think only of plundering them, and when they whose office it is to rebuke sin flatter all who will feed them plentifully, we have the state of society described by the prophet in

, and may know that terrible calamities are at hand-- calamities for which God will hold the rulers and teachers responsible, who have turned justice into robbery, and truth into falsehood.  But even in such dark times God will raise up some bold reprovers of sin, whose labors in behalf of truth and righteousness shall not be in vain.

entries.title: Micah 3:2
segments: Their skin; the skin of my people; a figurative description of cruel oppression and robbery.

entries.title: Micah 3:4
segments: Then; in the time of their calamity, which has been foretold,
, and is again brought to view in 3.6,7,12.

entries.title: Micah 3:5
segments: That bite--and cry, Peace; that is, prophesy peace to him who will supply their mouths with food.

entries.title: Micah 3:6
segments: Night shall be unto you--not have a vision; God will so expose their falsehood, that their prentended visions shall cease.  This he did by his judgments, in direct opposition to their prophecies of peace.  Compare

entries.title: Micah 3:7
segments: Cover their lips; or, "beard," as a sign of mourning.  See note to

entries.title: Micah 3:8
segments: But truly I am full of power by the Spirit of the Lord; the prophet contrasts his spirit and messages with those of the false prophets.

entries.title: Micah 3:12
segments:
Be ploughed as a field; this awful threatening was fulfilled by the Chaldeans, and more fully by the Romans, who destroyed the city to its very foundations. 
 
  The mountain of the house; Moriah, on which the temple stood.
